name: What is the best order for an exterior remodel?

mainEntity.name: What is the correct order to do an exterior remodel so the project does not get reworked later?
mainEntity.text: What is the correct order to do an exterior remodel so the project does not get reworked later?

acceptedAnswer.text: The best exterior remodel order starts with planning, not demolition. First define the scope, budget, and design intent, then measure the home and confirm any permit requirements. After approvals, crews typically handle demolition, structural repairs, waterproofing, window and door installation, and flashing details before moving to finishes like stucco, siding, cladding, trim, and paint. Hardscape, lighting, and landscaping usually come later so they are not damaged by wall work or material staging. The most important rule is to complete water management before cosmetic finishes. If flashing, drainage, and weather barriers are not corrected first, new materials can trap water and create expensive hidden damage. On larger projects, coordinating the entry, façade, driveway, and yard together can prevent mismatched details. Homeowners should also confirm access, dumpster placement, staging space, and inspection milestones before work begins. The right sequence reduces rework, protects the home from weather, and keeps the final result cohesive.
acceptedAnswer.description: The usual order is design and scope, survey and measurements, permits, demolition, structural or framing repairs, waterproofing, windows and doors, exterior finishes, then paint, fixtures, and landscape touch-ups. Starting with the wrong sequence can damage finished work or hide problems behind new materials. Water management and flashing should be completed before decorative finishes.
